title: Owner saves reference .asd and .alc files from the DAW for the generated test WAVs
description:
## Intent
Real-format fixtures: sidecar files saved by the DAW itself, for the generated test WAVs. A machine cannot do this; the owner (or an agent driving the owner's DAW with permission) does, once.

## Steps (manual, in the DAW)
1. Generate the audio: `python3 scripts/daw-fixture-audio.py --out ~/daw-fixtures`.
2. For each WAV, drag it into an audio track, then:
   - `steady-120.wav`: warp on, mode Complex, set markers so beat 1.1.1 is the first downbeat (pickup before it); press the clip view's Save → `steady-120.wav.asd`. Drag the clip to the browser → `steady-120.alc`.
   - `steady-120.wav` again, edited: move the marker at bar 3 beat 1 later by about 100 ms, Save → `steady-120-edited.wav.asd` (rename after saving).
   - `tempo-change.wav`: markers at each beat including the one at beat 6.5; Save → `.asd`; also export `.alc`.
   - `detuned.wav`: mode Beats, detune -30 cents, loop 2 bars → `.alc`.
   - `free-time.wav`: warp off → `.asd` and `.alc`.
3. Write down the DAW version and, for each file, the markers the DAW shows (seconds, beat) in `fixtures/README.md` (table).
4. Put the sidecars (never the WAVs) in a folder the spike can read; M1 moves them into `crates/apricity-daw/tests/fixtures/`.

## Done when
Every file above exists, the README table lists the markers the DAW showed, and the DAW version is recorded. Comment the folder path here.

## Depends on
The fixture audio generator chore (same epic).
